Estimate angler trips from extrapolated effort

Source: R/creel-estimates-trip-density.R
estimate_angler_trips.Rd

Computes estimated trips by dividing extrapolated effort by the mean trip length per stratum, with Delta Method variance propagation (Powell 2007). This is a composable estimator: the effort object must be pre-computed via estimate_effort before calling this function.

The divisor is hours per trip, so the result comes back in whichever actor the effort was measured in: angler-hours give angler trips, party-hours give party trips. The returned unit field records which, and is NA when the effort's own unit was unknown. The method string is "angler-trips" in every case and so is not a guide to the actor.

Usage

estimate_angler_trips(effort, design, conf_level = 0.95, ...)

Arguments

effort

A creel_estimates object returned by estimate_effort. Must have a numeric estimate column and a se column in effort$estimates.

design

A creel_design object with interview data containing a trip duration column (set via add_interviews(trip_duration = ...)). Used to compute per-stratum mean trip length.

conf_level

Confidence level for confidence intervals. Default 0.95.

...

Reserved for future arguments.

Value

A creel_estimates object with method = "angler-trips" and variance_method = "delta". The estimates tibble contains:

by_vars columns

Any grouping columns from the effort object (if grouped).

estimate

Estimated trips per stratum (effort / mean trip length), in the actor the effort was measured in.

se

Standard error via Delta Method variance propagation.

ci_lower

Lower confidence interval bound.

ci_upper

Upper confidence interval bound.

n

Number of interviews contributing to mean trip length per stratum.

For grouped effort, an .overall row is appended with estimate = sum(stratum trips). Its se adds the stratum variances in quadrature when the effort rows are independent (ground counts). Aerial effort rows share the visibility correction and angler-to-people ratio, and GLMM rows also share model coefficients, so for those the covariance of the effort rows is used and each shared term enters the total once.

Grouping columns that are not character (numeric, factor, Date) are returned as character, so the .overall marker can share them.

Trip length

Trips are effort divided by mean trip length (Pollock et al. 1994, p. 175). That divisor has to be the mean length of completed trips, sampled without regard to how long they were, so:

  • Only complete trips (trip_status == "complete") enter it. An incomplete trip records the time fished so far, not a trip length.

  • Roving designs (interview_type = "roving") are refused. A roving clerk meets anglers in proportion to how long they fish (length-of-stay bias; Pollock et al. 1994, sec. 11.4; Robson 1961), and the time fished at interview cannot be inverted into a trip count (Hoenig et al. 1997). Pollock et al. (1994, p. 175): "an unbiased estimate of mean trip length cannot be obtained from a roving survey ... and must be achieved by other means."

  • Angler-hours are divided by hours per angler trip: every angler in a party of \(n\) makes one trip, so each trip length is weighted by its party size. Party-hours are divided by hours per party trip, unweighted. When the effort's unit is unknown and party sizes vary, the two divisors differ and nothing says which applies, so the call is refused; give add_counts() a period length to make the effort angler-hours.

  • Bus-route and ice interviews are weighted by their inclusion weights (.expansion / .pi_i; Jones and Pollock 2012), as their effort is.

On a design with more than one stratum, effort must be grouped by every stratum column, and the total across strata is the .overall row: \(\sum_h \hat{E}_h / \hat{L}_h\), built stratum by stratum as Pollock et al. (1994, sec. 15.3.3.6) build season catch. One trip length pooled across strata weights each stratum by its share of the interviewed trips, not of all trips. Sampling weekends more heavily than weekdays, or taking a fixed number of interviews per day however busy it is, then biases the total. On a simulated season it was off by -16% and +8% (GH #691). Ungrouped effort carries no per-stratum effort to weight by, so it is refused.

The mean is a ratio estimator on the interview survey design, so interviews on the same day are not treated as independent, and the confidence interval uses that design's degrees of freedom (days less strata) rather than the number of interviews.

References

Hoenig, J. M., Jones, C. M., Pollock, K. H., Robson, D. S., and Wade, D. L. (1997). Calculation of catch rate and total catch in roving surveys of anglers. Biometrics, 53(1), 306-317.

Jones, C. M., and Pollock, K. H. (2012). Recreational angler survey methods: estimation of effort, harvest, and released catch. In A. V. Zale, D. L. Parrish, and T. M. Sutton (eds.), Fisheries Techniques (3rd ed., pp. 883-919). American Fisheries Society.

Pollock, K. H., Jones, C. M., and Brown, T. L. (1994). Angler Survey Methods and Their Applications in Fisheries Management. American Fisheries Society Special Publication 25. Chapters 11 and 15.

Powell, L. A. (2007). Approximating variance of demographic parameters using the delta method. Journal of Wildlife Management, 71(3), 1018-1024.

Robson, D. S. (1961). On the statistical theory of a roving creel census of fishermen. Biometrics, 17(3), 415-437.

See also

estimate_effort, estimate_exploitation_rate

Examples

data(example_calendar)
data(example_counts)
data(example_interviews)
design <- creel_design(example_calendar, date = date, strata = day_type)
design <- add_counts(design, example_counts)
design <- add_interviews(design, example_interviews,
  catch = catch_total, effort = hours_fished, harvest = catch_kept,
  trip_status = trip_status, trip_duration = trip_duration
)
#> Warning: ! No `n_anglers` provided — assuming 1 angler per interview.
#> ℹ Pass `n_anglers = <column>` to use actual party sizes for angler-hour
#>   normalization.
#> ℹ If the interviews really are one angler each, pass `n_anglers = 1` to state
#>   that and silence this warning.
#> ℹ Added 22 interviews: 17 complete (77%), 5 incomplete (23%)
# Effort by stratum: the `.overall` row is the total across strata.
effort <- estimate_effort(design, by = day_type)
#> Warning: Instantaneous counts were expanded without a period length.
#> ℹ No `period_length_col` was supplied to `add_counts()`, so the estimate is the
#>   count column summed over days.
#> ! If that column holds an instantaneous angler count, the result is the anglers
#>   present at the counted moments, not angler-hours: a count becomes effort only
#>   when multiplied by its period length. The package cannot tell which unit the
#>   column is in.
#> ℹ Supply the period each count was randomised within: `add_counts(design,
#>   counts, period_length_col = <col>)`.
#> ℹ Repeats on this design are recorded, not printed: see `get_warnings()`.
estimate_angler_trips(effort, design)
#> 
#> ── Creel Survey Estimates ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Method: angler-trips
#> Variance: delta
#> Confidence level: 95%
#> Grouped by: day_type
#> Effort target: period_total
#> 
#> # A tibble: 3 × 6
#>   day_type estimate    se ci_lower ci_upper     n
#>   <chr>       <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl> <int>
#> 1 weekday      129.  15.6     94.5     163.    10
#> 2 weekend      186.  20.1    142.      230.     7
#> 3 .overall     315.  25.4    259.      371.    17
